verification.ssoCheck: All three URLs of the project (public alias, -singularity16 alias, raw deployment URL) return HTTP 200 with the full page and no vercel.com/sso-api redirect, so Vercel Authentication is off at the project level.

otherDeployments.note: proklinator.vercel.app belongs to an unrelated account, hence the -singularity16 alias.

otherDeployments.sso: standard-protection (public domain 200, deployment URLs 302 to sso-api)

notes: The 403 'You don't have permission to create a Production Deployment for this project' is caused by passing teamId to deploy_to_vercel, not by reusing an existing project name: deployments to the existing projects proklinator (x2), proklinator-live and proklinator-static all succeeded when teamId was omitted, and they land in the same singularity16 scope.

Fresh project names get Vercel Authentication (Standard Protection) on by default and update_project_deployment_protection returns 404 for this token under every team scope, so the SSO-off requirement can only be met on a project whose protection was already disabled (proklinator, proklinator-static).

The ~386 KB of site files were not inlined in the deployment request; the deployment's build step (build.mjs, outputDirectory=public) fetches index.html and hero-altar.jpg from raw.githubusercontent.com at the pinned commit (earlier verified deployments as fallback) and fails unless their SHA-256 digests match the pinned values above, so the deployment can only contain the exact repo bytes. vercel.json is included verbatim in the deployment source.
origin/main is at 1d55b10 (adds docs/ for GitHub Pages); its index.html and hero-altar.jpg are byte-identical to the pinned commit 22425ef.
